content.comment_body: Hello. I'm trying to create a User Defined Function (UDF) and get the error message: "Insufficient resources to paste the blocks." What is the maximum number of blocks allowed in a UDF? Here are the resources used in the project: Function Blocks 235 / 400 REM[BINARY_DATA_REMOVED] 8 / 250 Digital Inputs 2 / 24 Digital Outputs 2 / 20 Flag 34 / 64 Analog Inputs 0 / 8 Text Box 19 / 50 Text contents 19 / 50 Analog outputs 0 / 8 Program memory 2932 / 8500 Block names 12 / 100 Analog flags 20 / 64 Cursor keys 4 / 4 Shift register 0 / 4 Shift register bits 0 / 32 Open connectors 2 / 64 Function keys 0 / 4 Network inputs 6 / 64 Network analog inputs 0 / 32 UDF types 4 / 16 UDF instances 10 / 64 Data Log 0 / 1 Network outputs 4 / 64 Network analog outputs 0 / 16 Analog Filters 0 / 8 Layout memory 29002 / 30000 Maximum nesting depth info: NI5-B031-B109-B126-B015-B127-B016 Tmr PER PROM-B129-B086-U001(Maximum:5)-U002(Maximum:4)-U003(Maximum:4)-U005(Maximum:4)-B028-U004 active KUM(Maximum:3)-B039 active KUM-AM1
The error message means that copying UDFs results in block numbers that exceed what's allowed inside a UDF. I've read somewhere that the highest block number for a UDF may be 199.
Thank you! How can I resolve this? Should I try highlighting the blocks, pasting them onto a new blank sheet, and somehow renumbering them?

I do not believe that rebuilding the UDF will fix the issue. The system automatically assigns the next available block numbers when copying and pasting blocks or UDFs. For example: If you create a UDF with block numbers B001 to B021 and insert it, those numbers are assigned. If you insert the same UDF again, it gets block numbers B022 to B042, and so forth as you continue programming or inserting more UDFs.
I found a related topic in the German section of the forum. In one reply, it was suggested to submit a Support Request for your case.

It seems like the problem could be due to the LSC version. I tested this with [product_name] V8.2.1 by inserting a UDF with 8 blocks into an empty diagram and copying it 49 times. This used up all 400 function blocks, with no block number errors initially. Only after trying to insert another UDF copy did the error appear, which makes sense since all function blocks were already occupied.
Try uploading your program and the UDFs themselves instead of just images. There might be something that can be corrected or changed. Regards, [user_name]
Thanks! Of course! I’m surprised I didn’t think of that myself.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience an 'Insufficient resources to paste the blocks' error when creating or copying User Defined Functions in the programming environment. This typically happens when resource limits, notably block counts or numbering, are reached. The unclear documentation or restrictions related to block numbers within UDFs leads to confusion about resolving these issues.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish to create and duplicate UDFs without facing resource restrictions they don't understand, and want clearer guidelines or tools to handle block numbering and usage limitations.
